## TransferStore interface

The persistent, subject-bound record of binary transfers. See the module documentation for its guarantees.

**Signature:**

```typescript
interface TransferStore
```

Method

<tbody><tr><td>

[allocateTemporaryCopy(subject, options)](./runtime.transferstore.allocatetemporarycopy.md)

</td><td>

Mint a temporary copy for a local read by `subject`<!-- -->: the store creates an empty file at a fresh path of its own choosing and records it. The caller writes the copy's bytes there and releases it when done; the sweep removes it after its lifetime. The store never accepts a caller-chosen path, so it can only ever delete files it named.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[close()](./runtime.transferstore.close.md)

</td><td>

Close the database. Safe to call more than once; every other method fails once the store is closed. A receive still in flight is not waited for: it fails, and its upload stays `receiving` (like a process ending mid-receive) until it expires and the sweep removes it.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[consumeUpload(subject, uploadId)](./runtime.transferstore.consumeupload.md)

</td><td>

Consume a completely received upload for one operation. The consumption is recorded first, so the id is spent whatever this call's outcome.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[createUpload(subject, options)](./runtime.transferstore.createupload.md)

</td><td>

Create an upload slot for `subject`<!-- -->.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[issueDownloadLink(subject, grantToken)](./runtime.transferstore.issuedownloadlink.md)

</td><td>

Exchange a grant presented by `subject` for a fresh download link to its file. Every call issues a new link.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[issueGrant(subject, file)](./runtime.transferstore.issuegrant.md)

</td><td>

Issue a grant for a file an authorized operation returned to `subject`<!-- -->. The grant is reusable until it expires.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[receiveUpload(subject, uploadId, bytes, options)](./runtime.transferstore.receiveupload.md)

</td><td>

Receive an upload's bytes and mark it complete. An upload is received once; an interrupted receive (the source throws or the signal aborts) deletes the partial bytes and leaves the upload awaiting bytes again. If the process ends mid-receive, nothing can reset the upload: it stays `receiving` (unreceivable, and holding one of the subject's outstanding slots) until it expires and the sweep removes it with its partial bytes.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[redeemDownloadLink(token)](./runtime.transferstore.redeemdownloadlink.md)

</td><td>

Resolve a download link to the file it delivers. The link is the bearer capability, so no subject is involved.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[redeemGrant(subject, token)](./runtime.transferstore.redeemgrant.md)

</td><td>

Look up a grant presented by `subject`<!-- -->.

</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[sweep()](./runtime.transferstore.sweep.md)

</td><td>

Remove expired grants, download links, and uploads (with their bytes), released and long-abandoned consumed uploads, and expired temporary copies (files and records).

</td></tr>
